images.title: Lift from 2 to −3
images.purpose: Show that the lift going from floor 2 down to floor −3 moves 5 floors down, which is −3 − 2 = −5.
images.composition: One tall vertical column of floors on the left of centre with one long arrow beside it and one line of text to the right, much white space.
images.exact_structure: One vertical column of 6 equal square floors in grey #6B7280 outline, stacked, numbered from the top 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3. Floor 2 filled teal #0072B2, floor −3 filled amber #E69F00. Beside the column, one long arrow in reddish purple #CC79A7 from floor 2 down to floor −3, labelled 5 floors down. Exactly 6 floors, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Target minus start gives the movement.
images.description: A column of 6 floors from 2 to −3 with a downward arrow of 5 floors, and −3 − 2 = −5.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the floors the arrow crosses and say the target minus the start.

image_decisions.why: The lift movement is a picture idea; one column with one arrow carries it.
